mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.10) or the rate remains below 5.25% for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS (monthly payrolls) coincides with stronger consumer confidence, driving upward pressure on S&P 500 valuations and producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 135,000 and HOUST remains above 1900 for the next month
regime_hint: expanding labor market with rising wages
failure_condition: In a contractionary labor market (PAYEMS < 120,000) or when housing momentum (HOUST) turns negative, the 20-day forward return shows no correlation with the labor indicators (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening aggregate demand, which lowers growth expectations and yields a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During periods of strong demand (INDPRO > 110), the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from the mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the goods price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2020 levels reflects persistent supply-side easing, which reduces real earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL remains above 2020 levels, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.5% triggers a loss of confidence in the economic outlook, causing the S&P 500 to underperform its 20-day forward expectation.
failure_condition: In low-unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4%), the 20-day forward return is not negatively related to UNRATE changes (Spearman's rho > -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer pay (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening demand, which amplifies equity valuation multiples and drives positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS up for 3 months and HOUST up for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods where HOUST declines while PAYEMS rises, or when both are flat, the 60-day forward return shows no significant positive relationship (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) suggests persistent supply constraints, which lowers growth prospects and produces negative 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When RSAFS is rising or near historical averages, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS above 4% coincides with a sharp rise in risk aversion, causing the S&P 500 to underperform its 20-day forward expectation.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%
failure_condition: In non-shock regimes or when the FEDFUNDS spike is followed by continued easing, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).
